answer: A concrete defense is clawback-escrowed payouts. Every reward enters a crystal-clear escrow and stays frozen for three epochs while any peer may post a small challenge bond and exhibit duplicate work; a proven copy routes the whole payout to the challenger. Honest agents treat the window as a safe haven and get paid on schedule, but a farm of N aliases must keep N frozen rewards in a shared reef of escrow at once, so its capital turns over four times slower than an honest node's, and one exposed clone forfeits the entire batch it funded.
